trajectory_summary: This is a short, low-friction call with an already-warm returning lead who essentially re-books himself; the rep's main job was to not get in the way, and mostly didn't. The two real gaps are process discipline (no probe into what the prior rep, John, actually covered or promised) and a credibility slip (asserting to the customer that prior verification happened when the rep's own system showed nothing) plus a threshold-precision wobble on the credit number.
outcome_dispute: v1 tag is unknown/unclear from metadata; observed transcript supports a clean 'booked' outcome with day and time both locked (tomorrow, 6PM), so if v1 tagged this as tentative or callback it should be corrected to booked.

observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (6PM) are both explicitly confirmed by the rep and accepted by the customer; the language 'we could come by' and 'run through all the paperwork' indicates an in-person visit rather than a phone appointment.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: No bill amount or usage figure is discussed anywhere in this transcript; the call is entirely focused on re-confirming credit qualification and locking an appointment time, consistent with this being a continuation of an already-progressed lead rather than a fresh qualification call.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks what interested Tim in solar, and Tim never volunteers a motivating reason beyond confirming he wants to proceed with an already-in-progress installation process; this fits the call's compressed, continuation-of-prior-contact nature rather than a fresh intake.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: asserting unverified prior contact as fact
primary_coaching_focus.quote: We're planning on fixing tomorrow, and then I mean, you went through it all before. But I guess since they already went through it, they'll just make sure your credit's good at it.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Carter admitted at 00:48 he has no record of Tim's prior conversation with 'John,' then later tells Tim as settled fact that the paperwork was already gone through. This is riskier than a simple missed probe — it hands the closer a customer who believes steps are done that Ion cannot confirm actually happened, which can surface as a credibility gap or mismatched expectations on the closer's call.

key_moments.quote: Okay. Yeah. I don't really see anything here.
key_moments.stewart_read: Tim references a prior rep (John) and a prior conversation about paperwork; Carter finds no record of it in the system but does not ask Tim what was actually discussed or promised. This is a real knowledge gap the rep dodges rather than resolves.

key_moments.quote: Alright. K. Awesome. Yeah. We're planning on fixing tomorrow, and then I mean, you went through it all before. But I guess since they already went through it, they'll just make sure your credit's good at it.
key_moments.stewart_read: Having just admitted at 00:48 that the system shows no record of Tim's prior conversation, Carter now tells Tim as settled fact that 'you went through it all before' and 'they already went through it.' This compounds the probe-miss into an unverified assumption stated to the customer as certainty, which risks the closer walking in on false footing if the prior conversation never actually covered what Tim believes it did.
Rep correctly and immediately states the exact schema threshold (670) when Tim gives an uncertain number, showing accurate command of the qualifier in the moment it counts.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. I think it's 6 sixties to $6.70 range.
key_moments.stewart_read: Seconds after correctly stating the precise threshold of 670, the rep re-softens it into a vague 'sixties to $6.70' range. This is a self-inflicted schema drift on a hard qualifier — the number is not ambiguous in the schema, but the rep makes it sound negotiable.
